chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold objection against seven: the child, the one who died during the period between two prophets, the elderly senile man who lived during the period of prophecy, the simple-minded person, the mentally ill, the deaf and the dumb. Each of these will plead their case to Allah, the Mighty and High.

He said: So Allah, the Mighty and High, will send to them a messenger who will light a fire for them and say: 'Verily, your Lord has commanded you to jump into it.' Thus, whoever jumps in it, it will become cool, and a means of peace for him, and whoever resists will be driven to the Hell.

key_terms.الْأَبْلَهِ: The simple-minded / naturally intelligent but not learned
key_terms.بَيْنَ النَّبِيِّينَ: Between the prophets (period of inter-prophetic gap)

ai.seo_question: How does Allah ensure justice for those who missed the prophets or lacked full mental capacity?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith to illustrate the principle of *Adl* (Divine Justice), emphasizing that God does not punish those who were genuinely incapable of understanding or accepting the message due to specific conditions like age, mental capacity, or historical timing. The narrative of the 'test' with the fire serves as a practical demonstration of obedience, where the fire's transformation into 'coolness and peace' for the obedient mirrors the story of Ibrahim, reinforcing that divine mercy is contingent upon sincere submission to God's command.
